summary: Create a board-owned read/composition slice. The RSC page calls one server-only board DAL entrypoint; that entrypoint authenticates the actor, injects adapters over the existing trusted work-items and labels APIs, and invokes a pure board use-case. Neither existing capability imports the board or the other capability.

tree.purpose: Thin async RSC. Parses URL-owned filters, calls getBoardPage(), and renders the returned serializable view model.
Streaming fallback for the board read.
Safe UI error boundary with retry; never displays raw server errors.
Board schemas/types: statuses, columns, cards, visible label summaries, and invariants.
Pure orchestration and board policy: remove archived items, group by status, collect label IDs, resolve labels, reject unresolved/invisible labels, and build the view model.
Board-owned WorkItemsReader and LabelsReader interfaces; no imports from concrete adapters.
Implements WorkItemsReader by calling the work-items public server API and mapping its DTOs into board input types.
Implements LabelsReader using the labels batch-read public API; maps only actor-visible labels.
server-only composition root. Verifies the session, constructs actor/request context and adapters, calls loadBoard(), reports failures, and returns a DTO.
Server-rendered board presentation receiving only the board view model.
Existing capability-owned trusted read surface, exporting listBoardCandidates(context). Returns authorized item DTOs including archived/status/label IDs, never persistence rows.
Existing capability-owned trusted batch surface, exporting resolveVisibleLabels(context, ids). Enforces label visibility and returns only authorized label DTOs.
Policy and orchestration tests using fake ports.
Contract/mapping tests against each capability public surface.
Authentication, dependency composition, safe failure mapping, and telemetry ownership tests.
Column, empty-state, and visible-label rendering tests.
Real authenticated flow, authorization isolation, archived-item exclusion, grouping, inaccessible-label exclusion, and error-boundary behavior.

flows: Read: src/app/board/page.tsx → board/dal/get-board-page.ts → verifySession() → loadBoard({workItems, labels}, actor).
Work items: loadBoard → WorkItemsReader.list(actor) → work-items/public/server.listBoardCandidates(actor) → work-items-owned use-case/port/persistence. Work-items applies its own item authorization.

Labels: after archived items are removed, loadBoard deduplicates referenced label IDs → LabelsReader.resolveVisible(actor, ids) → labels/public/server.resolveVisibleLabels(actor, ids) → labels-owned use-case/port/persistence. Use one capped batch request, not per-card calls.

Composition: loadBoard indexes returned labels, removes every label association not present in the authorized result, groups remaining items by board status, and returns immutable serializable columns/cards.
Render: page.tsx passes the view model directly to BoardView. No internal HTTP request, Server Action, client store, or TanStack Query is needed.

decisions.choice: The board capability owns cross-capability orchestration and board-specific policy.
decisions.rationale: Grouping, archived-item exclusion, and label attachment change for board reasons and do not belong to either source capability.

decisions.choice: Board use-cases depend on board-owned ports; board outbound adapters depend on the public server surfaces of work-items and labels.
decisions.rationale: Work-items and labels remain independent and never import one another; concrete capability APIs do not leak into the board use-case.

decisions.choice: Expose narrow server-only DTO APIs under each capability's public/server.ts barrel.
decisions.rationale: This provides a stable contract while keeping persistence adapters, internal domain objects, and capability implementation details private.

decisions.choice: Authenticate once in the board DAL and re-enforce resource authorization inside each capability API.
decisions.rationale: Route protection is insufficient. Work-items decides which items are visible; labels decides which labels are visible. The board never trusts IDs merely because an item references them.

decisions.choice: Treat absent results from the authorized label batch as rejected and omit both their details and associations from the board DTO.
decisions.rationale: The rendered response must not reveal an inaccessible label's existence, name, color, or authorization status.

decisions.choice: Fail the complete board read if either capability has an unexpected dependency failure; use normal empty states only for successful empty results.
decisions.rationale: Rendering cards without trustworthy label-policy evaluation could produce a misleading or unsafe partial board.

decisions.choice: The board DAL reports caught unexpected composition failures once with request ID, operation, and capability tags, then throws a sanitized error for app/board/error.tsx.
decisions.rationale: Use-cases remain telemetry-independent, raw exceptions are not exposed, and duplicate capture is avoided. Expected unauthenticated/forbidden outcomes are mapped without error-level reporting.

decisions.choice: Do not add a board aggregate cache initially; allow each capability to own and invalidate its actor/tenant-scoped read cache.
decisions.rationale: This preserves independent changeability and avoids a cross-capability invalidation contract. Add an aggregate cache only after defining tags for both dependencies and every mutation path.

decisions.choice: Test policy with fake ports, public-surface mapping with adapter contracts, DAL security separately, and the full authorization flow in E2E.
decisions.rationale: Each test protects the layer that owns the behavior and avoids coupling pure orchestration tests to persistence.

risks: The public DTO contracts must be versioned or changed compatibly; otherwise independent capability changes can break the board adapter.
Label ID batches require schema caps and deduplication. Large boards may need paginated work-item reads and chunked label resolution.
Status values unknown to the board need an explicit policy, preferably mapping to an “unknown” fallback column rather than silently dropping authorized items.
If capability APIs use different actor or tenant semantics, define one server-only authenticated request-context contract before composing them.
